name: Brine Whisper
geological_features: Planet-wide ocean with no exposed landmass
Deep hydrothermal vent fields along a single tectonic ridge
Thick saline ice shelves at the poles
specific_features: Bioluminescent microbial blooms visible from orbit as shifting pale-green patterns
The Murmur — a persistent low-frequency acoustic phenomenon generated by vent activity
Hyper-saline brine pools on the ocean floor that form distinct liquid-in-liquid lakes
description: Brine Whisper is a small oceanic world wrapped in a single unbroken ocean averaging six kilometers in depth. Its dense atmosphere presses down on the water's surface, creating a perpetual overcast of pearlescent clouds that filter the system's starlight into a diffuse, silvery glow. No land breaks the surface — only the endless, gently rolling sea.

The atmosphere is heavy and humid, carrying a faint mineral tang that settles on every surface. Below the cloud layer, the ocean hums with a persistent low-frequency resonance generated by the planet's hydrothermal vents, a sound the first survey teams named the Murmur and which has never been fully explained by simple geological models.

Microbial life thrives in extraordinary density around the vent fields, forming vast bioluminescent colonies that pulse with slow, coordinated rhythms visible even from low orbit. Xenobiologists have cataloged over three hundred distinct microbial species, several of which produce compounds with significant pharmaceutical potential — a discovery that has drawn considerable corporate interest to this otherwise unremarkable world.

The hyper-saline brine pools on the ocean floor represent some of the most extreme biochemical environments ever documented, and the organisms that inhabit their margins may hold the key to understanding abiogenesis in high-salinity conditions. Research stations float on the surface in small clusters, their crews enduring the isolation and the Murmur's ceaseless drone for the chance to study life at its most fundamental.
